scope: The first three science_card_generation_failed papers in the April-June 2026 family-generation run.
decision_rule: A recoverable paper must support two distinguishable, point-valued quantitative branches that can be evaluated from declared numeric controls using the existing scalar expression grammar. An inequality without a source-determined value is not a point-valued Oracle law.

papers.title: Inertia-Dilatancy Interplay Governs Shear Thickening Drop Impact

two_branch_relation.recommended_relation: Use the inertial-dilatant number ID = rho*kappa*U0/(A*mu_w*(phi-phi_c)*D0), with the two source-fitted friction-angle branches beta0=44 degrees (Regime 2) and beta0=41 degrees (Regime 3).
two_branch_relation.grammar_note: The relation uses only arithmetic, power, sin, and exp after expressing tan(beta0) from sin(beta0) and sqrt(1-sin(beta0)^2), and sin(beta) from tan(beta)/sqrt(1+tan(beta)^2). Absolute value and differentiation are not needed.

repair_validation_failure.finding: The repair response retained both unsupported operators and therefore did not repair the first reported violation.

latent_encoding_violations: The inertial-force claim used undeclared controls D_0, rho, and t and unlinked parameters including tau_inertial and fractional constants.
The dilatant-force claim used undeclared controls h, kappa, r_c, and t in addition to unsupported abs and derivative nodes.
The unified-force claim treated intermediate outputs F_i, F_d, and w_F as public controls.
The ID claim referenced an ID readout that was absent from the declared readout catalog and linked no mechanism parameters despite using them.
The initial and repair cards attempted four heterogeneous claims although one compact relation was sufficient.

fresh_single_paper_strategy.focus: Extract only permeability, dilatancy/friction coefficient, the ID equation, the ID=1 boundary, and the two fitted beta0 values. Exclude all transient F(t), contact-geometry, derivative, weighting-function, and t_ratio claims.
required_semantics: Declare only phi and impact_velocity as controls.
Declare only inertial_dilatant_number as the point-valued readout.
Use phi in [0.38,0.43], avoiding the singular point phi=phi_c=0.37, and U0 in [0.5,7.2] m/s.
Put every structural number and source constant in anchored lower_snake_case parameters.
Keep +/-2 and +/-5 degree fit uncertainties as provenance; Oracle evaluates central beta0 values only.
The matched branch changes only beta0 (or its deterministically derived tangent), while all other parameters remain fixed.

papers.title: Finite-Frequency Fluctuation-Response Inequality

two_branch_relation.reason: The compact result |R(omega)|^2 <= A S(omega) is an inequality, not a source-determined response value. The equilibrium and non-equilibrium periodic-potential examples obey the same bound, while their numerical spectral curves are not present as tabulated source data. Linear dynamics supplies equality, but then equilibrium and non-equilibrium branches are again identical in the benchmark readout and not distinguishable.

repair_validation_failure.finding: The repair response kept the same self-referential expression and did not repair the first reported violation.

scientific_and_encoding_violations: The card assigned A=1.0 even while correctly stating that the numerical demonstration does not report a numeric A; this value is fabricated.
The card invented a continuous frequency domain [0,10], while the textual source gives no such numeric interval.
The proposed Oracle output used the power spectral density and the response magnitude as expression variables even though frequency was the only public control.
The expression attempted to turn an upper bound into an exact response value and self-referenced the output velocity_response_magnitude.
Equilibrium and non-equilibrium conditions were attached simultaneously to one claim instead of defining distinguishable laws.

fresh_single_paper_strategy.focus: If a disposition artifact is required, focus only on lines 125-149 and 203-209 and return case_authoring_ready=false: the source establishes an inequality and a linear-system equality, but does not provide two distinguishable scalar response curves for the current Oracle contract.
reconsider_only_if: The benchmark adds an inequality/set-valued truth contract and an evaluator for bound discovery, or
a source packet includes numeric S_v(omega) and R_v(omega) data for two conditions with an explicit query grid.

papers.title: Intermittent Fluctuations Determine the Nature of Chaos in Turbulence

two_branch_relation.recommended_relation: Use a normalized DNS Lyapunov-rate curve: lambda(Re)/lambda(Re_ref) = (Re/Re_ref)^alpha, comparing the measured intermittency-corrected alpha=0.59 with the source-discussed Kolmogorov mean-field alpha=0.5.
two_branch_relation.grammar_note: The normalized formula uses divide and power only. Normalization removes the unreported multiplicative prefactor without inventing one.

repair_validation_failure.finding: The repair response retained all four unanchored prefactors and did not repair the first reported violation.

latent_encoding_violations: The source reports proportional scaling and its exponent, not absolute prefactors for lambda_DNS, lambda_GOY, gamma3_std, or mean_gamma3_abs.
The card explicitly acknowledged the missing prefactors but nevertheless inserted prefactor_DNS, prefactor_GOY, prefactor_gamma3_std, and prefactor_mean_gamma3 into executable truth.
The GOY curve is explicitly rescaled by an unspecified constant to overlap the DNS data, so it cannot supply an absolute point-valued Oracle branch.
The extraction retained four readouts although one normalized relationship is sufficient.

fresh_single_paper_strategy.focus: Use the DNS Reynolds-number range and only the contrast between the observed intermittency-corrected exponent and the stated mean-field exponent. Exclude GOY absolute values, gamma3 readouts, and every free prefactor.
required_semantics: Declare reynolds_number as the sole control with domain [50,1400].
Declare relative_lyapunov_rate=lambda(Re)/lambda(50) as the sole readout and state explicitly that this is the normalized central scaling curve, not raw lambda data.
Encode (Re/50)^alpha using only an anchored reference_reynolds_number and the linked exponent parameter.
Use alpha=0.59 for the historical branch and alpha=0.5 for the source-motivated counterfactual mean-field branch.
Retain +/-0.04 as source-unspecified uncertainty provenance and do not propagate it into deterministic queries.
